title: Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair
read_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19066v3 (21 August 2026; FSE 2026 Companion / industry-track paper; full 10,618-word extraction)
datasets: 120 Google-internal GITS bug reports across six languages: C++ 36, Dart 2, Go 17, Java 34, Kotlin 14, Python 17. Each has an internal bug report, source/fix and developer-written fail-to-pass BRT; exact bug contents and repositories are private.
No SWT-Bench, Defects4J, BugsInPy or other public task benchmark is evaluated; SWT-Bench is related work only.
task: A proprietary Google Passerine agent jointly generates a fix and bug-reproduction test in one patch. It compares Fix-only and BRT-only against Freeform, test-first TDD, and test-last TLD cogeneration, using execution/reviewer feedback and test-aware patch selectors. A BRT is plausible when it fails on the buggy source and passes on the developer oracle fix; a plausible fix passes the held-out oracle BRT.
input_setting: Google GITS issue report and internal source repository are provided to the agent. The agent has code-search, file-view/edit and test-run tools, up to 25 steps per trajectory; 20 trajectories per bug/config. Gemini 2.5 Pro is used at temperature 0.2/top-p 0.95; the spec-based reviewer uses Gemini 2.5 Pro at temperature 0.0/top-p 0.95. Internal repo, model prompts and tool integration are not public.
author_artifact_url: No code, data, or replication-package URL is linked by the paper. Official FSE program page: https://conf.researchr.org/details/fse-2026/fse-2026-industry-papers/35/Dynamic-Cogeneration-of-Bug-Reproduction-Test-in-Agentic-Program-Repair
author_relationship_evidence: Paper authors are Google researchers; sections 2 and 4 explicitly describe their deployed Google-internal Passerine APR system and 120 bugs from Google Issue Tracking System. The paper does not link code/data. Exact-title/GitHub searches and the official FSE conference page found no author artifact; CatalyzeX offers only a code-request link, not source. Thus the methods and data are internal/private.
source_commit_or_archive: No public source commit or archive found. Paper PDF/HTML is public under CC BY 4.0, but the Passerine agent, Google GITS cohort, execution traces and patch data are not released. Checked paper links, official FSE program page and exact-title/GitHub source searches; no implementation or dataset package located. No code was executed.
license: Paper: CC BY 4.0. No software or task-data license because no author implementation/dataset artifact is public.
exact_models: Gemini 2.5 Pro, temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95 for agent generation.
Gemini 2.5 Pro, temperature 0.0, top-p 0.95 for the spec-based patch reviewer.
No model snapshot/revision or released weights are specified.
weights_status: Hosted Google Gemini API; no weights or exact immutable model revision. The system and prompts/tool integrations are proprietary; no independent local-model route or public dataset exists for running Qwen on the same cohort.
evaluation_route: Read complete 10,618-word v3 paper (1,002 lines), including all methods, result tables, internal data conditions, failure analysis, threats and references; SHA-256 above. Evaluates five configurations (Fix-only, BRT-only, Freeform, TDD, TLD), 20 trajectories per bug with 25 steps each across 120 Google bugs. Cogeneration keeps plausible-fix and plausible-BRT generation broadly comparable with separate pipelines; Freeform has highest joint pass & plausibleBRT@20. Ranked test-aware selector yields 0.16 precision/0.71 recall for selecting patches with both plausible fix and BRT vs default selector 0.08/0.57. Failure analysis identifies test edits cleaned up before submission, wrong debugging hypotheses/step exhaustion, and fix-test mutual overfitting. Exact reproduction and own-model evaluation on the same set are impossible without Google data/source; no run performed.
blockers: All 120 task instances come from Google's private GITS and internal repositories; issue descriptions, code, fixes, tests, trajectories and labels are unavailable publicly.
Passerine agent, tool APIs, system prompts, validation and patch-selection infrastructure are proprietary/not linked.
Only Gemini 2.5 Pro is reported; no immutable model revision, weights or provider-neutral configuration is released.
No public SWT-Bench/Defects4J/BugsInPy experiment cohort can substitute without creating a new experiment, which would not reproduce the paper.
concept_fit: Very high conceptual fit for studying joint bug-fix/BRT generation and root-cause-driven tool behavior. The failure analysis attributes failed trajectories to test cleanup, wrong debugging hypotheses/tool friction, and fix-test overfitting; it explores TDD/TLD/Freeform order and test-aware selection. However, it does not publish an externally usable root-cause taxonomy for the underlying software faults, and all empirical evidence is private Google data.
recommendation: Keep as a high-value conceptual prior for whether tests should be generated alongside fixes and for analyzing agentic failure causes, but do not select as a reproducible base or own-model benchmark. Its Google-only data and Passerine implementation block exact replication; the paper reports no Defects4J, BugsInPy or SWT-Bench experiment. Use its concepts (TDD/TLD/Freeform comparison, test-presence-aware patch selection, and failure categories: discarded tests, debugging loops, fix-test overfitting) to inform research questions and qualitative analysis only. Prefer #89 Multi-SWT-Bench or #98 TDD-Bench-Java when an open own-model evaluation is required. No code/model run.
supporting_locations: Paper Sections 2–4: internal Passerine system, 120 GITS tasks across six languages, Gemini model, 20 trajectories × 25-step limit, Fix/BRT/TDD/TLD/Freeform settings.
Paper Tables 2–6: action behavior, conditional cogeneration probabilities, BRT signal and test-aware selector precision/recall.
Paper Section 6: manual/LLM trajectory analysis; failures include dropped test changes, debugging loops and fix-BRT interference/overfitting.
Paper Section 8: explicit threat that Google proprietary engineering environment may not generalize.
No source/data/reproducibility URL appears in the paper; official FSE page links publication information only.
